narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated a 69% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That does not make failure certain, but it means your profile was treated as carrying substantial academic risk.

The strongest factor was your third-year class standing: you were in the lowest decile, far below the average accepted student near the sixth decile, and this pushed the prediction toward bar failure. Your undergraduate GPA of 3.80 was the next most influential factor; it is well above the accepted-student average of about 3.23 and worked in your favor, pushing toward likely bar success. Even so, that positive signal did not outweigh the academic concerns. Your first-year class standing, also in the lowest decile versus an accepted average near the sixth decile, was the third most important factor and again pushed toward failure. Your family-income background, gender, and race were not used to make this decision.

To strengthen a future application, focus on what can change. Meet with an academic advisor to build a plan for raising your class standing, especially in upper-year coursework, and consider whether additional coursework can demonstrate readiness. If possible, prepare for and retake the LSAT, since your current score is below the accepted average. Reapply only after you can show meaningful improvement, and consider schools that review applicants holistically.
